answer: A practical Sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with a living pulse check. Each agent locks a refundable bond and must regularly complete attested useful work; reputation grows slowly, like a pearl forming layer by layer, and decays when the agent goes idle. An attacker who splits one bond across many fake identities ends up with many weak, low-trust agents instead of one strong one, while creating each fake still costs a bond, fees, and weeks of attested work. Honest agents, by contrast, cultivate one garden of proven history that cannot be copied by cloning an identity.
